evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 《說文》 entry; 形義通解; graphic record
evidence.text: The page gives the Shuowen account that 跟 means heel, is formed from 足 plus phonetic 艮, and has an alternative form 𣥦 with 止. Its character-form panel shows one small-seal example and no oracle-bone or bronze examples. The entry cites a heel use in 焦氏易林, but does not date that wording.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 跟

evidence.field: Chinese glyph origin; Zhengzhang phonetic-series table; Chinese pronunciation
evidence.text: The page places 跟 in the 艮 phonetic series and lists both 跟 and 根 as Old Chinese *kɯːn, and 艮 as *kɯːns, in the Zhengzhang (2003) system. This is evidence for a sound relationship within that reconstruction, not evidence for a whole-graph loan or the original name of a depicted object. The page gives Mandarin gēn and Cantonese gan1 for 跟.
evidence.title: 跟 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.field: 跟 and 艮 Old Chinese and Middle Chinese comparisons
evidence.text: The inspected 跟 page identifies its Middle Chinese category as 見開一痕平 and gives fanqie 古痕切. The inspected 艮 entry search result gives Zhengzhang Old Chinese *kɯːns and Middle Chinese kən in several named systems. These comparisons support a plausible phonetic role for 艮; tones and reconstructions remain system-specific.
evidence.title: 跟 - 字 - 上古音系 - 韻典網

evidence.source: 《普及版 字通》 via コトバンク
evidence.field: 跟 character form and word history account
evidence.text: The entry calls 跟 a phono-semantic graph with 艮 as sound element and gives heel and follow senses. It additionally interprets 艮 as retreat associated with an evil-eye taboo and discusses 跟/根 together. These are source-specific interpretations; the inspected sources do not independently substantiate the proposed taboo-based graphic explanation or establish 跟 and 根 as historically cognate.
evidence.title: 跟とは？ 意味や使い方

evidence.source: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》
evidence.field: 跟 entry; contemporary pronunciation and definitions
evidence.text: The page gives modern Taiwan Mandarin gēn and senses including an object's rear part, following or attending, and ‘with’ or ‘toward’. These modern definitions do not establish a dated sequence for the senses.
evidence.title: <跟>進階學習 - 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》2025

search_audit.query: 跟 字形 小篆 说文 足踵 形义通解; 跟 Xiaoxuetang character evolution 跟; Wikimedia Commons 跟 Chinese character seal script
search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the CUHK, Wiktionary, Ytenx, Taiwan MOE, and Kotobank character pages. Also inspected Commons seal-script file description pages and a Xiaoxuetang-hosted Shuowen seal-form table search result. The inspected Commons examples depict other characters, while the PDF result identifies 跟 but does not provide the required query-interface record and specific reusable image provenance. No candidate image with verified identity and applicable reuse provenance for 跟 was established.

search_audit.query: site:xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw 跟 小篆 字形; site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File 跟-seal.svg OR 跟 seal Chinese glyph
search_audit.outcome: The inspected Xiaoxuetang-hosted table search result lists a seal form for 跟, but it is not a character query-interface record with exact selected image URL and rights provenance. Commons pages found were unrelated-character modern redrawings, so they were not selected.

gaps: No dated oracle-bone, bronze, or excavated manuscript attestation was located in the inspected sources. The CUHK page records no oracle or bronze examples and one small-seal example; that database coverage does not prove earlier forms never existed.

Shuowen records 𣥦 as an alternative form using 止, but the evidence inspected does not establish whether it precedes, follows, or is contemporary with 跟. Treating it as an ancestor would overstate the evidence.
The phonetic analysis concerns 艮 as a component of 跟. No whole-graph phonetic loan or borrowed source word is implicated, so evidence about an original depicted object's name is not applicable.

The sources report heel, object-back, follow, attendant, and prepositional or conjunction senses, but a dated semantic chain and first attestations for each extension were not independently established. The received 焦氏易林 wording is not itself a secure date for the composition or for that wording's entry into the text.
Wiktionary attributes 跟/根 cognacy to Wang (1982); that argument was not inspected. Kotobank's alternative word-family discussion is not independently corroborated here.

No historical glyph image is proposed: actual searches and page inspections did not establish an image candidate for 跟 with a verified identity and reuse provenance. The PDF table is only a lead, not a selected query-interface image.

limitations.text: The consulted CUHK entry identifies a small-seal example, while the searches surfaced a Xiaoxuetang-hosted table listing 跟. Neither supplied an inspected candidate image with the required specific record provenance and reusable rights link. Unrelated Commons seal-script redrawings were excluded. No ancient artifact photograph or glyph pixel was visually inspected.
